questions.question: What must you add so that @Scheduled methods actually run?
questions.explanation: @EnableScheduling starts the scheduler. Without it the @Scheduled annotations are ignored silently.

questions.question: What is the difference between fixedRate and fixedDelay?
options: fixedRate counts from the start of a run, fixedDelay counts from the end of the last run
questions.explanation: fixedRate keeps a steady start-to-start gap. fixedDelay waits the given time after the previous run finished.

questions.question: A job has @Scheduled(cron = "0 0 2 * * *"). When does it run?
questions.explanation: The fields are second, minute, hour, day, month, weekday. Second 0, minute 0, hour 2 means 2:00 AM every day.

questions.question: Two scheduled jobs use the default settings. Job A sleeps 5 seconds each run. What happens to Job B, due every second?
options: It runs on time on its own thread
It waits, because the default scheduler has one thread
questions.explanation: By default all scheduled jobs share one thread, so a slow job delays the others.

questions.question: A developer writes @Scheduled(fixedRate = 1000) public String report(int day). The job never runs and startup reports an error. What is wrong?
options: A scheduled method must take no arguments, and it should return void
Strings cannot be used in components
questions.explanation: Spring calls the method itself, so it cannot supply an argument. Scheduled methods take no parameters and return void.
